item: The finished in-memory rollup is checkpointed once before the serve check (R164), which shrinks it about 7x and lets the wider windows answer
summary: An in-memory rollup stays uncompressed until something checkpoints it. columnar.compact(con) now runs CHECKPOINT right after the build and before the serve check. Measured with no other cursor reading (rerun_compact.py): resident 529.5 to 55 MiB at 12 M mentions and 456.1 to 73.2 MiB at 16 M in under a second, the 30-day top-terms query's peak 719 to 244 and 701 to 315 MiB, and the all-history top terms (0 rows before, out of memory) answer at both sizes with identical per-term counts. An allocation FatalException at the checkpoint is a duckdb-limit stop at stage compact (sizes read before it, class name only); any other fatal is the unusable-instance failure; any other error leaves the rollup serving uncompacted and status()[last_build][compact] says compacted false with the error class. Also corrects the earlier claim that the resident size varies by 300 MiB between runs: it was a second polling cursor in the benchmark, not DuckDB (OPEN_QUEUE, lesson item 5).
